---
title: "Robustness"
---

Two questions about the headline decomposition: does the ranking of the channels
survive a different way of attributing their contributions (Shapley), and does it
survive perturbing the model's key frictions (sensitivity sweeps)?

## Shapley decomposition

The headline marginals activate the channels in a fixed order (U → R → C), which
under-credits whichever channel is added last. The Shapley value averages each
channel's contribution over all six activation orders. Below, canonical (sequential)
against Shapley, for each channel, at four intensities. The sign is the same under both
rules; what changes is the *ranking* — the central-bank channel is systematically
under-credited by the sequential order at moderate stress, and dominates in the tail.

```{ojs}
shap = FileAttachment("../data/shapley_decomp.csv").csv({typed: true})
shapLong = shap.flatMap(r => [
  {intensity: r.intensity, channel: "Unsecured",   rule: "Canonical", value: r.canonical_U},
  {intensity: r.intensity, channel: "Unsecured",   rule: "Shapley",   value: r.shapley_U},
  {intensity: r.intensity, channel: "Repo",        rule: "Canonical", value: r.canonical_R},
  {intensity: r.intensity, channel: "Repo",        rule: "Shapley",   value: r.shapley_R},
  {intensity: r.intensity, channel: "CB credit",   rule: "Canonical", value: r.canonical_C},
  {intensity: r.intensity, channel: "CB credit",   rule: "Shapley",   value: r.shapley_C}
])
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 860, height: 380, marginBottom: 50,
  x: {label: null, tickFormat: d => "I=" + d},
  y: {label: "Contribution (pp of CET1)", grid: true},
  fx: {label: null},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["Canonical", "Shapley"], label: "Attribution"},
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(shapLong, {fx: "channel", x: "intensity", y: "value", fill: "rule",
                         dx: 0, sort: {fx: null}}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
})
```

## Sensitivity sweeps

Each sweep perturbs one friction one-at-a-time and re-measures the channel marginals
Δ_U / Δ_R / Δ_C (percentage points of CET1) at the focal intensity. The dashed line
marks the headline calibration. Across all four, the **sign and ordering of the
marginals are preserved** — repo positive and largest, central-bank credit positive,
unsecured small.

```{ojs}
sweeps = [
  {file: "sensitivity_freeze.csv", key: "nr", label: "Repo-freeze threshold (banks running)"},
  {file: "sensitivity_fsa.csv",    key: "amp", label: "Fire-sale amplifier"},
  {file: "sensitivity_rho.csv",    key: "rho", label: "Repo-congestion elasticity"},
  {file: "sensitivity_run_k1.csv", key: "k1", label: "Depositor-run intensity"}
]
freeze = FileAttachment("../data/sensitivity_freeze.csv").csv({typed: true})
fsa    = FileAttachment("../data/sensitivity_fsa.csv").csv({typed: true})
rho    = FileAttachment("../data/sensitivity_rho.csv").csv({typed: true})
runk1  = FileAttachment("../data/sensitivity_run_k1.csv").csv({typed: true})
sweepData = ({sensitivity_freeze: freeze, sensitivity_fsa: fsa, sensitivity_rho: rho, sensitivity_run_k1: runk1})
```

```{ojs}
function sweepPlot(rows, key, label) {
  const long = rows.flatMap(r => [
    {x: r[key], channel: "Δ_U", value: r.delta_U_pp, headline: r.headline},
    {x: r[key], channel: "Δ_R", value: r.delta_R_pp, headline: r.headline},
    {x: r[key], channel: "Δ_C", value: r.delta_C_pp, headline: r.headline}
  ])
  const hx = rows.filter(r => r.headline === true || r.headline === "TRUE").map(r => r[key])
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 420, height: 260, grid: true, marginBottom: 40,
    x: {label: label},
    y: {label: "Marginal (pp)"},
    color: {legend: true, label: "Channel"},
    marks: [
      hx.length ? Plot.ruleX(hx, {stroke: "grey", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}) : null,
      Plot.line(long, {x: "x", y: "value", stroke: "channel", marker: "circle"}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ].filter(Boolean)
  })
}
```

::: {layout-ncol=2}
```{ojs}
sweepPlot(freeze.filter(r => r.nu === 20), "nr", "Repo-freeze threshold")
```

```{ojs}
sweepPlot(fsa, "amp", "Fire-sale amplifier")
```

```{ojs}
sweepPlot(rho, "rho", "Repo-congestion elasticity")
```

```{ojs}
sweepPlot(runk1, "k1", "Depositor-run intensity")
```
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Notes
Shapley values average each channel's marginal over the six activation orderings of
{U, R, C}; standard errors follow by exact propagation from the arm-level cross-seed
errors. Sensitivity sweeps vary one friction at a time at the focal intensity, ten
seeds per stochastic cell; the freeze panel fixes the unsecured-freeze threshold at its
headline value and varies the repo-freeze threshold. All aggregates over the whole
67-bank sample.
:::
